lesson.grammar_point: too + adjective (too expensive / too big) + How about + price? for offers

listenings.text: Hi Marlene, it is Selin, from the cooking class. You told me you want to visit the Grand Bazaar tomorrow. Here are my tips. The bazaar is huge, with more than four thousand shops, so wear comfortable shoes. In many shops you can haggle, but be friendly and smile. When the seller says a price, do not say yes at once. Say: it is too expensive for me, how about a lower price? The seller makes a new offer, and you make an offer too. If the price is still too high, say thank you and walk away. Sometimes the seller calls you back with a good deal. And drink the tea if they offer it. Have fun!

Welcome to the Grand Bazaar, one of the oldest covered markets in the world. It opened more than five hundred years ago. Today it has sixty-one streets, so please stay close to the group. In this part you can see carpets and lamps. The carpets have beautiful patterns, and some of them are made of silk. A small silk carpet can take many months to make, so it is not cheap. The colorful glass lamps are very popular, and they are easy to carry. The bazaar is closed on Sundays. We have one hour for shopping, and we meet at the main gate at twelve thirty.

extra_audio.text: First, you walk into the Grand Bazaar and you look at the carpets. Then the seller says the price, and you say it is too expensive. Next, you make an offer: how about two hundred euros? After that, the seller makes a new offer, and you haggle a little more. Finally, you agree on a good deal, and you buy a small silk carpet.
